answer: One defense is hardware-bound identity: each agent must prove its key lives inside a distinct secure enclave, like a single opal set in its own orchard row rather than a copied gem. The enclave signs a fresh challenge, and the network accepts only one identity per attestation key, so a bridge of cheap software copies collapses at registration. An attacker must buy one real device per fake identity, turning free cloning into a per-unit hardware cost that makes large Sybil fleets uneconomical.
